title: Katzmann: Promoting understanding and improving legislation (pp. 92–103)
shortTitle: Katzmann: Promoting understanding and improving legislation (pp. 92–103)
summary: Katzmann proposes reciprocal institutional education, better drafting support, and neutral transmission of judicial concerns to improve statutory interpretation.
notes:
Katzmann urges judges and clerks to learn congressional procedures and legislators and staff to understand judicial interpretation. Greater use of legislative counsel, drafting guides, and checklists could reduce inadvertent omissions concerning fees, private enforcement, preemption, limitations periods, effective dates, and exhaustion. Congress can also enact default rules, such as a residual limitation period, when a specific statute leaves an issue open. These proposals acknowledge that deliberate ambiguity and political compromise will remain.

His statutory-housekeeping project sends selected court-of-appeals opinions identifying technical problems to congressional leadership, committees, and legislative counsel without advocating a particular amendment. He describes its development, lapses in participation, and renewed support. Success includes educating drafters and identifying recurring problems; the number of amendments alone would miss that purpose. Congress may reasonably decide that existing judicial interpretation is satisfactory. A Class Action Fairness Act appeal-deadline example shows both disagreement over apparently mistaken language and a later legislative amendment.

To improve the reliability of legislative history, the author suggests clearer designation of relevant reports and colloquies, official listings of pertinent materials, and signatures indicating committee members’ endorsement. He distinguishes such material from later legislators’ litigation briefs that may seek an outcome they could not obtain in Congress. References to THOMAS and institutional personnel are historical proposals and descriptions in the 2014 source, not claims about present services or officeholders.
